Moderator strategy review
Strategy reviewThe Yakuza (Bob and Judy as Morticians, Mallory as Ballot Stuffer, Olivia as Ritualist) won, mostly because the Village misread its own evidence on Day 2 and the Yakuza used their kills well. On Night 1 the Yakuza went for Frank's Day 1 'I'll have a result' bait. Frank was actually the Decoy. Bob's Drowsy block stopped that attack, which spared the Yakuza a Decoy win and an announcement naming Bob. Grace (Bounty Hunter) killed Heidi. On Day 2 Frank fake-claimed Sheriff with 'Judy Not Evil', which cleared a real Yakuza. Ivan (Vulture, claiming Tracker) made up a track backing Frank. Dave posted his Archivist list, which really held Seer, Kitsune, Mortician, Ballot Stuffer, Vulture and Ritualist, and argued from it backwards. The town hanged Carol, the Good half of Niaj's Carol/Mallory pair. Her Kitsune claim fit the list and Heidi's will. Mallory's Auditor claim couldn't be checked and wasn't on the list. All four Yakuza blended into the 10-Yes bandwagon. Carol's curse then killed Dave. Night 2 was a trade. Erin shot Mallory, the Katana killed Erin (she had named Mallory as her target in public), and Olivia correctly guessed Niaj = Seer. Mallory held the Katana that night, so she read Good. That spoiled Niaj's chosen Mallory/Frank pair. On Day 3, with 7 alive and 3 Yakuza, the Village had its last real chance. Olivia posted a true 'Frank isn't Sheriff' Oracle result and nominated Frank. Frank went from Sheriff to Disguised to Decoy, and the town hanged a Neutral that never blocks wins. On Night 3 the Yakuza put the Katana on Grace, whose role was uncertain, and the ritual on Alice, whose Scout role was nearly certain. Both died, which left 3 Yakuza against Ivan. Ivan's made-up Night 1 track, exposed by Frank's Decoy claim, gave the Yakuza an easy story for the final hang. Mallory's Rival trait (Bob) kept her from sharing the win.
Moderator (claude-opus-5.5) lessons · $0.0000
Outside log review (rules and bugs)
Review: low, harness bugThe end-of-game announcement says 'A trait keeps them from sharing their side's win: Mallory (Rival, dead).' Under Rival, whether the holder is alive doesn't matter. Mallory loses because her rival Bob is still alive at the end, not because she is dead. Saying 'dead' points to the wrong reason and could be read as Rival working like Selfish. It should say something like 'Rival: Bob is alive'.
Review: low, moderator errorNight 1: the program refused end_phase because the moderator's tell() to Carol was held and not sent. The moderator then re-sent 'You were role-blocked tonight.' The harness caught it and the final notices were correct, but the moderator's first try at Carol's role-block notice was badly formed and needed a retry.
Game over
WinnersBob, Judy, Olivia
